subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: Should Telegram local Bot API migrations reset polling offsets by apiRoot and treat deleteWebhook 400 Logged out as a non-fatal migration state?
rationale: The source path is clear, but choosing automatic endpoint-based offset reset and any 400 Logged out tolerance affects upgrade behavior, failure visibility, and Telegram auth safety.

options.title: Endpoint-aware reset and cooldown tolerance
options.body: Reset or invalidate offsets when the normalized apiRoot changes, and continue polling for a narrowly matched Logged out cooldown response with an explicit diagnostic and live local Bot API proof.

options.title: Document manual migration only
options.body: Leave runtime fail-closed behavior mostly unchanged and document that operators must clear the offset and wait out logOut cooldown before switching apiRoot.

options.title: Keep deleteWebhook fail-closed
options.body: Fix only offset scoping while preserving all non-network deleteWebhook failures as fatal startup errors.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware reset and cooldown tolerance
recommendation.body: Reset or invalidate offsets when the normalized apiRoot changes, and continue polling for a narrowly matched Logged out cooldown response with an explicit diagnostic and live local Bot API proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the Telegram state migration surface and have current-history signal on the affected offset/runtime files.
